subject: Bridging Observify edge agent with Redwood runtime — compatibility & next steps
messages:
From: Samantha Ortiz <samantha@observify.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Cc: partners@observify.ai
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Observify edge agent — integration primer and spec

Hi Rishi / Ben,

Thanks again for the intro call earlier this week. Per our discussion, I wanted to surface the high-level spec for the Observify edge agent and outline a proposed lightweight integration path so Redwood can ingest metrics/traces via an OTLP-forwarding adapter or direct ingestion into your Dedicated pools.

Key points:
- Agent mode: local collection -> OTLP gRPC (v0.19) + optional compressed HTTP fallback
- Two runtime modes: "gateway" (single-hop OTLP relay) and "sidecar" (per-host adapter).
- Our agent keeps fine-grained metadata and requires preservation of original trace IDs and span attributes for business filtering.

Attachments: observify-agent-specs.pdf (protocols, ports, TLS profile)

We'd love to understand the minimum runtime guarantees Redwood needs for (a) keeping span semantics intact, and (b) supporting our proposed prefix caching strategy for high-throughput mobile telemetry.

Proposed next step: a short technical sync with Laura and your infra runtime lead to validate kernel/quantization impacts and whether a small shim in the agent is preferable to a runtime adapter inside Redwood. Are you available Friday 11am PT?

Thanks,
Samantha Ortiz
Head of Integrations, Observify
[Attachment: observify-agent-specs.pdf (PDF)]

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Ortiz <samantha@observify.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Observify edge agent — integration primer and spec

Samantha — thanks for the doc and the clear summary. Helpful.

Laura — looping you in for a quick compatibility read. A couple of things we'd like to confirm before the call:
1) OTLP versioning — we support v0.19 but our runtime has a few internal expectations about resource attributes (service.name, deployment.environment) that we sometimes synthesize at the gateway. Would Observify be OK if Redwood added a small enrichment header instead of modifying spans?
2) Prefix caching — sounds like it could align with our prefix/KV cache model, but we need to measure utility vs cache memory cost. If Observify can publish a 48h tokenized sample trace set (anonymized), we can run a short experiment on Dedicated to quantify hit rates.
3) TLS handshake/profile — your spec lists mTLS optional; for Private deployments customers will require mutual TLS and HSM-backed cert management. Any constraints there?

Ben — can you own the commercial ask (mutual action plan + SOW skeleton) if the tech checks? Laura — can you run a quick read of the PDF and attach any gap notes?

I can do Friday 11am PT.

— Rishi
Director, Partner Integrations
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Samantha Ortiz <samantha@observify.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 09:33:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Observify edge agent — integration primer and spec

On Thu, Apr 1, 2027 at 5:05 PM Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Samantha — thanks for the doc and the clear summary. Helpful.

Quick initial technical notes after skimming the spec (see attached matrix for details):
- OTLP: compatibility looks good for gRPC v0.19. We do need to validate batch sizes and max message bytes; your agent default of 16MB batch could trigger fragmentation in our streaming paths. Recommend a 4MB default with explicit batching config.
- IDs/Attributes: preserving trace/span IDs is fine. Do not alter sampling flags at the gateway — we rely on those for downstream cost accounting. If enrichment is necessary, prefer a metadata header (x-redwood-enrich: true) so spans are unchanged.
- Prefix caching: promising, but requires a small shim in our runtime to expose per-request cache hints; we've prototyped this already (internal PR) and can turn it on for an initial pilot.
- Quantization/kernel: Observify's hints about short-span hotspots might benefit from our 8-bit KV cache paths; we should shadow-run with quantized tokens to ensure fidelity.

I've attached an "agent-compatibility-matrix.xlsx" with specific gaps and a short checklist for a 2-hour pilot: runtime flags, TLS cert rotation, batch tuning, and sample dataset exchange.

[Attachment: agent-compatibility-matrix.xlsx (XLSX)]

Happy to take the Friday slot. Suggest the agenda: 15m goals + spec alignment, 30m tech deep dive, 15m pilot plan and deliverables.

— Laura
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Ortiz <samantha@observify.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 11:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Observify edge agent — integration primer and spec

Samantha / team — thanks. From the commercial side, assuming tech greenlights the pilot, proposed commercial touchpoints:
- Mutual action plan (MAP) with a 6-week pilot milestone, success criteria tied to trace fidelity and <10% additional per-token cost on pilot traffic.
- SOW draft to cover support levels for Dedicated and Private (we'll include an integration engineering hour budget).
- Early access promo: 3 months of reduced metering for pilot environments (subject to leadership approval).

I've started a MAP draft and dropped it into our shared drive: https://drive.redwood.com/Shared/partners/observify/integration-notes (file: mutual-action-plan-draft.md). Also created a HubSpot opportunity MP-4812 to track the partner integration funnel.

If the team agrees, I'll prepare a short DocuSign for the pilot SOW (low-friction) and route to your legal.

— Ben
Senior Strategic Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Links: https://drive.redwood.com/Shared/partners/observify/integration-notes, HubSpot MP-4812]

Action items I heard:
- Observify: prep and upload anonymized 48h trace sample to your shared drive (will do by EOD Monday)
- Redwood (Laura): run compatibility checklist and confirm batch defaults to 4MB for the pilot
- Redwood (Ben): share MAP draft and pilot SOW for review
- Scheduling: Friday 11am PT technical sync (invite forthcoming)

Looking forward to it — excited about the possibility of a tight integration that keeps fidelity and reduces downstream cost for joint customers.

Best,
Samantha Ortiz
Head of Integrations, Observify
